mainTopic: Whether a money-sinner may testify in capital cases (רבי מאיר vs. רבי יוסי, settled by a סתם משנה), the list of relatives disqualified from testifying, and the Torah source for that rule.
overview: The amud opens with the end of בר חמא's trial. The witnesses against him were said to have stolen, which is a money-type sin. רב אבא בר יעקב objects that disqualifying them works only according to רבי מאיר, while the הלכה usually follows רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי says someone disqualified in money matters can still testify in capital cases. רב פפי answers that an unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר here. After rejecting one possible source, the גמרא proves this from the משנה listing dice players, lenders on interest and others as unfit wherever a woman is unfit. בר חמא is freed and thanks רב פפי. A new משנה then lists the relatives who cannot testify or judge, gives רבי יוסי's earlier version, and discusses former relatives and רבי יהודה's view on friends and enemies. The גמרא learns the relatives rule from 'לא יומתו אבות על בנים', meaning not through each other's testimony. It then explains that children are punished for their parents' sins only when they continue them, and that ערבות applies when people could have protested and did not.

steps.title: The end of the testimony: a spear handle
steps.stepSummary: The text opens in the middle of the story. These words finish describing what one of the witnesses against בר חמא was accused of stealing: the handle of a spear.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...the handle of a spear.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the story in the middle. These two words finish the earlier report that one of the witnesses was accused of stealing a spear handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stealing an object is a money-type sin. That is why the next step asks whether a money-type sin can disqualify someone from testifying in a capital case like this one.

keyTerms.meaning: Handle
Spear

phrases.english: The handle of a spear.
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from before: it names what one of the witnesses was said to have stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of בר חמא from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualifying testimony is about theft, which is a money-type sin.

steps.title: Do you hold like רבי מאיר? The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אבא בר יעקב challenges בר חמא. Disqualifying these witnesses for a money sin only works according to רבי מאיר. But the rule is that in a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי says an עד זומם in money cases may still testify in capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are you thinking? Do you hold like רבי מאיר? Between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי says: someone caught as a lying witness in a money case is still allowed to testify in capital cases!
steps.whatsHappening: בר חמא is being challenged. He is told that his way of disqualifying the witnesses goes against the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that someone disqualified because of a money matter is disqualified for capital cases too. רבי יוסי says he stays valid for capital cases. Since the general rule is that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר, the witnesses against בר חמא should still count.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your reasoning? What do you hold?
The final ruling follows רבי יוסי
Was caught as an עד זומם (a lying witness proven false by other witnesses)
Money cases
Capital cases (life-and-death cases)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not say a lying witness is a good person. He only says that being caught lying in a money case does not disqualify him from capital cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole סוגיא: the general rule says follow רבי יוסי, so we need a strong reason to follow רבי מאיר here.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your thinking?
phrases.notes: This is רב אבא בר יעקב speaking to בר חמא.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Meir?
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei:
the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Yosei says, doesn't he:
if he was proven a lying witness in money cases,
he is fit for capital cases!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges using a money-type theft to disqualify witnesses in a capital case.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר חמא's attempt to disqualify the witnesses because of theft.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That disqualification works only according to רבי מאיר, but the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who keeps such a witness valid for capital cases.

steps.title: רב פפי: a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר here
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי answers that the rule 'הלכה כרבי יוסי' applies only when there is no unattributed משנה following רבי מאיר. Here there is one, so we follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to him: That rule applies only where the תנא did not give us an unnamed משנה that follows רבי מאיר. Here, the תנא did give us an unnamed משנה that follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי defends בר חמא's position. He limits the general rule about following רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה states a law without a name, that usually signals the accepted ruling. A סתם משנה like רבי מאיר is stronger than the general rule of following רבי יוסי. So on this issue the הלכה would follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only...
The תנא taught us without naming anyone (a סתם משנה)
The teacher of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a סתם משנה can override a general rule about whom the הלכה follows.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said to him:
This applies only

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלָא סְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: where the tanna did not teach us an unnamed ruling like Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא סְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Here the tanna taught us an unnamed ruling like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא סְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the הלכה always follows רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not when a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר, and here one does.

steps.title: Which משנה follows רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this unnamed משנה following רבי מאיר is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רב פפי for his source. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא tries out a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי's answer depends on there really being a סתם משנה like רבי מאיר. The גמרא now wants to identify it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רב פפי's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר on this issue.

steps.title: Trying out a source: 'Anyone fit for capital cases is fit for money cases'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה that says anyone fit to judge capital cases is fit to judge money cases. It reasons that this cannot be רבי יוסי, because for him a money-case עד זומם is fit for capital cases but not for money cases. So the משנה must be רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is from what we learned: 'Anyone who is fit to judge capital cases is fit to judge money cases.' Whose view is this? If you say it is רבי יוסי, there is the lying witness in money matters, who is fit for capital cases but unfit for money cases! Rather, isn't it רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible source for רב פפי's claim. It shows that this משנה does not fit רבי יוסי, so it seems to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says anyone fit for capital cases is fit for money cases, with no exceptions. According to רבי יוסי there is an exception: a money-case עד זומם is fit for capital cases but not money cases. Since the משנה allows no exception, it seems to follow רבי מאיר, who disqualifies him for both.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
That we learned in a משנה
Fit to judge
Whose view is it?
A witness proven to be lying by other witnesses
Rather, isn't it...? (pushes toward a conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אילימא hints that this suggestion may later be rejected. Don't treat it as the final answer yet.

phrases.english: If you say from what we learned:
Anyone who is fit to judge capital cases
is fit to judge money cases.
Whose view is it?
If you say it is Rabbi Yosei,
there is the lying witness in money matters,
who is fit for capital cases
and unfit for money cases!
Rather, isn't it Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question 'ממאי?'
steps.raayaObject: רב פפי's claim that a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'כל הראוי לדון דיני נפשות ראוי לדון דיני ממונות', which allows no exception and so seems not to fit רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Maybe that משנה is about family background, not sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 5. The משנה about judges may be talking about people disqualified by lineage, so it tells us nothing about sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know it is רבי מאיר? Maybe the משנה is talking about people who are disqualified because of their family background!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the source it just suggested. It says that משנה might not be about sinners at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the משנה ('whoever can judge capital cases can judge money cases') was about someone who sinned with money. If the משנה is about family-background disqualifications, then the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי never comes up. So the משנה could match anyone's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? How can you be sure?
Perhaps, maybe
People disqualified because of their family background (lineage)
It is talking about, it refers to

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know that this משנה follows רבי מאיר?

phrases.english: Perhaps it is talking about those disqualified because of lineage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 5 by giving the משנה a different subject.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the judges משנה as the unnamed source that follows רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה was about sinners. It could just as easily be about people disqualified by family background.

steps.title: The second half of that משנה shows it is about lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the rejection. The second half of the same משנה only makes sense if it is about lineage, so the first half is about lineage too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, look at the end of that משנה: 'Some are fit to judge money cases but not capital cases.' Why wouldn't such a person be fit for capital cases? If he was caught as an עד זומם in a capital case, could he judge money cases? Everyone agrees he is disqualified! So the end must be about lineage, and the beginning is about lineage too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection from step 6. It uses the second half of the משנה to show the whole משנה is talking about lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half speaks of someone fit for money cases but not capital cases. A sinner cannot fit that description, because an עד זומם in a capital case is disqualified from everything, and everyone agrees on that. So that clause must be about lineage, and the first clause should be read the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (a way of proving a point by showing the other option fails)
The latter part (end clause) of a משנה
Was made into an עד זומם (shown to be a false, plotting witness)
Everyone agrees
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: This proof only works if both halves of the משנה talk about the same kind of disqualification. The end clause cannot be about sinners, so the beginning is read as lineage too.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
There is one fit to judge money cases
but not fit to judge capital cases,
why is he not fit?
One who was made an עד זומם in a capital case,
is he fit to judge money cases?
But everyone agrees he is disqualified!
Rather, it is talking about disqualification due to lineage.
Here too it is talking about disqualification due to lineage.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the first half of the משנה, the one step 5 tried to use.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, סֵיפָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the rejection in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the judges משנה is talking about lineage and not about sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end clause of the same משנה, which cannot refer to a sinner, because a capital-case עד זומם is disqualified from everything according to all opinions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the first proposed source completely, so the גמרא must still find an unnamed משנה that follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A new source: the list of people unfit to testify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different unnamed משנה. It lists people disqualified from testifying and says they are unfit for any testimony a woman is unfit for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is where the תנא taught us an unnamed ruling, as we learned: These are disqualified: one who plays dice, those who lend with interest, those who fly pigeons, those who trade in שביעית produce, and slaves. This is the rule: any testimony a woman is not fit for, they are not fit for either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question from step 4. It quotes a משנה listing people who cannot testify. In the next step it will show that this משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the people listed are disqualified because of sins involving money. The key line is the general rule: wherever a woman cannot testify, they cannot testify either. The proof in the next step depends on that line.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught us without naming who said it (an unnamed ruling)
Dice (gambling)
Interest on a loan
Those who fly (race) pigeons
Those who do business with produce of the שמיטה year
This is the general rule

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הָכָא קָא סָתַם לַן תְּנָא,
phrases.english: Rather, here the תנא taught us an unnamed ruling,
as we learned in a משנה:
These are the ones who are disqualified:
one who plays with dice,
and those who lend with interest,
and those who fly pigeons,
and those who trade in Sabbatical-year produce,
and slaves.
This is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֵדוּת שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לָהּ,
phrases.english: any testimony for which a woman is not fit,
they too are not fit for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָכָא קָא סָתַם לַן תְּנָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source was rejected, the גמרא offers a new answer to the question in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is the unnamed משנה that follows רבי מאיר (from step 4)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה listing people unfit to testify, whose rule ties their disqualification to wherever a woman is unfit.

steps.title: This משנה can only be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The rule 'wherever a woman is unfit, they are unfit' includes capital cases. According to רבי יוסי, money sinners could still testify in capital cases. So the משנה must be רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say רבי יוסי, there is testimony in capital cases that a woman is not fit for, yet according to him these people would be fit for it! So isn't it רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the משנה from step 8 follows רבי מאיר. This finishes the search that began in step 4 and supports רב פפי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman cannot testify in capital cases. The משנה says these money sinners cannot testify wherever a woman cannot, so they are unfit for capital cases too. רבי יוסי allows them in capital cases, so the משנה cannot be his. It must be רבי מאיר, and an unnamed משנה following him means the הלכה follows רבי מאיר here.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is it?
If you say
But there is (a case that doesn't fit)
Rather, is it not? (leading to the only option left)

steps.whatToRemember: The unnamed משנה listing those unfit to testify follows רבי מאיר. Because of that, we follow רבי מאיר and not רבי יוסי here, just as רב פפי said. So the witness against בר חמא, who was shown to have committed a money sin, is unfit even in a capital case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This supports רב פפי's answer in step 3. An unnamed משנה can override the usual rule that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי against רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
If you say it is רבי יוסי,
but there is testimony in capital cases
for which a woman is not fit,
and they are fit for it?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the money sinners from the list, who are fit for capital cases according to רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not רבי מאיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the משנה quoted in step 8 can only fit רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That the unnamed משנה of disqualified witnesses follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that these people are unfit wherever a woman is unfit. That includes capital cases, which רבי יוסי would not accept.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר, so the הלכה follows him, and money sinners are disqualified from capital testimony too.

steps.title: בר חמא thanks רב פפי
steps.stepSummary: The story ends. The witness against בר חמא was disqualified, so בר חמא was freed, and he showed רב פפי deep thanks.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר חמא got up, kissed רב פפי on his feet, and took on himself to pay רב פפי's tax for all his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story about בר חמא. Since the ruling followed רבי מאיר, the witness against him was disqualified, and he showed great gratitude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps showed that an unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר. So a person who sins with money is unfit to testify even in capital cases. That ruling knocked out a witness in בר חמא's murder case, so his life was saved, and this line shows how thankful he was.

keyTerms.meaning: He kissed him on his feet, a sign of deep respect and thanks
A head tax paid to the government

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר: someone who sins with money, such as by lending with interest, is unfit to testify even in capital cases.

phrases.english: Bar Ḥama arose,
kissed him on his feet,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב פפי, the one who ruled like רבי מאיר and so disqualified the witness.

phrases.english: and took upon himself to pay his tax for all of his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by applying the conclusion that the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling follows רבי מאיר, the witness who sinned with money is out, and בר חמא is acquitted.

steps.title: The list of relatives who cannot testify or judge
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the relatives who are disqualified, and says how far the disqualification reaches to their sons and sons-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the relatives: his brother, his father's brother, his mother's brother, his sister's husband, the husband of his father's sister, the husband of his mother's sister, his mother's husband, his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law. These people, their sons, and their sons-in-law are all included. His stepson is included only by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists exactly which relatives are disqualified from being witnesses or judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list covers blood relatives, such as brothers and uncles, and relatives by marriage, such as the husbands of sisters and aunts, the father-in-law, and the brother-in-law. The sons and sons-in-law of all of these are also disqualified. The stepson is the exception: only he is disqualified, not his own children.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives who are disqualified from testifying or judging
His father-in-law
His brother-in-law, meaning the husband of his wife's sister
His stepson, his wife's son from another man

steps.confusionAlert: The word לְבַדּוֹ ("alone") applies only to the stepson. For everyone else on the list, their sons and sons-in-law are disqualified too.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the relatives:
his brother, and his father's brother, and his mother's brother,
and his sister's husband,
and the husband of his father's sister,
and the husband of his mother's sister,
and his mother's husband, and his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law.
They, and their sons, and their sons-in-law,
and his stepson alone.
phrases.notes: The stepson is disqualified, but his sons and sons-in-law are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: disqualified relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed relatives, along with their sons and sons-in-law, are disqualified. A stepson is disqualified only by himself.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the earlier version of the list
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the list above is רבי עקיבא's version. The earlier version disqualified only the uncle, the uncle's son, and anyone fit to inherit, based on the relationship at the time of the trial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: This is רבי עקיבא's version of the משנה. But the first version said: his uncle, his uncle's son, and anyone fit to inherit from him, and anyone related to him at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי tells us the list we just read is not the original. He gives the older, shorter version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, only relatives who could inherit were disqualified. Those are relatives through the father, so relatives through the mother were not included. רבי עקיבא's version added more relatives. The last phrase adds that the relationship is measured by the time of the trial, which sets up the next ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, earlier version of the teaching
His uncle, here his father's brother
Someone fit to inherit from him
At that time, meaning the time of the trial

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: זוֹ מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: This is Rabbi Akiva's version of the mishna,
but the first version of the mishna is:
his uncle and the son of his uncle
and anyone who is fit to inherit from him,
and anyone who is related to him at that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: זוֹ מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲבָל מִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, earlier version of the list in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first version, only the paternal uncle, his son, and anyone fit to inherit were disqualified, and the relationship is judged at the time of the trial.

steps.title: Someone who is no longer related may testify
steps.stepSummary: If someone was a relative but the relationship ended, he is fit to testify or judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a relative and then stopped being related, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on a person whose family tie has ended, for example a son-in-law whose wife died or who divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the idea that the relationship is measured at the time of the trial. If the tie no longer exists then, the person is no longer disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Became unrelated, the relationship ended
Fit, allowed to testify or judge

phrases.english: If he was a relative and became unrelated,
he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה קָרוֹב וְנִתְרַחֵק, הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule that the relationship is judged at the time of the trial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A former relative whose tie has ended is fit to testify.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: children keep the relationship alive
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the daughter died but left children with her husband, the husband is still considered a relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even if his daughter died, if her husband has children from her, he is still a relative.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the ruling just before. When children remain from the marriage, the former son-in-law is still treated as related.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the relationship ends when the marriage ends. רבי יהודה says the shared grandchildren keep the two families connected, so the son-in-law stays disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter died
Children from her

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if his daughter died,
phrases.notes: "His daughter" is the daughter of one side in the case. Her husband is the son-in-law whose status is being discussed.

phrases.english: and he has children from her,
he is a relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵתָה בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 13 in the case where children remain from the marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, children from the marriage keep the former son-in-law disqualified as a relative.
steps.whatToRemember: First opinion: once the family tie ends, the person is fit. רבי יהודה: if children remain from that marriage, he is still a relative.

steps.title: A friend and an enemy are also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה (continuing רבי יהודה's view) adds that someone who loves or hates a litigant cannot testify. It defines 'one who loves' as his groomsman, and 'one who hates' as anyone who refused to speak to him for three days out of hatred.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who loves and one who hates are disqualified. 'One who loves' means his groomsman. 'One who hates' means anyone who did not speak with him for three days out of hatred.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more kinds of disqualified people: a very close friend and an enemy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the list was about family. This step adds people who are disqualified because of strong feelings, not blood. It also gives exact definitions: the שושבין (groomsman) is the friend, and three days of angry silence makes someone an enemy.

keyTerms.meaning: One who loves, a close friend of a litigant
One who hates, an enemy of a litigant
Groomsman, the close friend who helps the groom at his wedding
Hatred, enmity

phrases.english: One who loves and one who hates.
"One who loves": this is his groomsman.
"One who hates": anyone who did not speak with him
for three days out of hatred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's additions to the list of disqualified people, moving from relatives to friends and enemies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this view, a groomsman (friend) and someone who refused to speak to a litigant for three days out of hatred (enemy) are disqualified as witnesses.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the friend and enemy rule
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that Jews are not suspected of lying in testimony just because of love or hatred.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The Jewish people are not suspected of that.
steps.whatsHappening: The other חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה and say friends and enemies can still testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives are disqualified by a rule of the Torah, not because we suspect them of lying. Friends and enemies are not on that list, and the חכמים refuse to assume a Jew would lie out of love or hate, so they stay fit to testify.

keyTerms.meaning: Were suspected
They said to him, the חכמים answering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים are saying relatives are trusted too. Relatives stay disqualified no matter what. The argument here is only about friends and enemies.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יהודה, who said friends and enemies are disqualified.

phrases.english: The Jewish people are not suspected of that.
phrases.notes: Meaning they are not suspected of lying in court because they love or hate someone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's addition of friend and enemy.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the disqualification of a friend and an enemy, not the relatives.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's rule assumes Jews would lie out of love or hate, and the חכמים do not accept that suspicion.
steps.whyThisMatters: The חכמים limit disqualification to the relatives on the list. A friend or an enemy, however close or bitter, may still testify.

steps.title: Where do we learn that relatives cannot testify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the Torah source for disqualifying relatives as witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that relatives are disqualified. This sets up the next steps, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a long list of relatives but no source. The גמרא now asks which פסוק teaches that relatives cannot testify.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: גמרא:
From where are these words learned?
phrases.notes: He means: where does the Torah teach that relatives cannot be witnesses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה by asking for the source of the relatives rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that relatives are disqualified from testifying.

steps.title: The answer begins with a פסוק about fathers and sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that quotes the פסוק 'Fathers shall not be put to death for children.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the חכמים taught: "Fathers shall not be put to death for children."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that points to a פסוק as the source. This step only quotes the פסוק; the next steps explain how it teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance this פסוק seems to be about punishment, not about witnesses. The ברייתא will show why it must really be about testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: As the חכמים taught, introducing a ברייתא
Fathers shall not be put to death for children

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק 'Fathers shall not be put to death for children', explained in the following steps.

steps.title: The plain meaning of the פסוק is already taught elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק is needed. If it means a father is not killed for his son's sin, the same פסוק already says 'every man shall be put to death for his own sin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק need to say this? If it is to teach that fathers are not killed for the sin of children, and children are not killed for the sin of fathers, it already says: "Every man shall be put to death for his own sin."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that the simple meaning of the פסוק is extra, since another phrase already teaches it. This prepares the way for a new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. Since 'every man for his own sin' already teaches that no one is punished for a relative's sin, the words 'fathers shall not be put to death for children' must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
For the sin of
Every man shall be put to death for his own sin

phrases.english: Why does the verse need to say this?

phrases.aramaic: אִם לְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת בַּעֲוֹן בָּנִים
phrases.english: If it is to teach that fathers are not put to death for the sin of children
and children not for the sin of fathers,
it is already stated:
"Every man shall be put to death for his own sin."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, דברים 24:16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the quoted פסוק is needed, setting up a new reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra words 'fathers shall not be put to death for children' come to teach, since their simple meaning is already covered.

steps.title: The פסוק means relatives cannot testify against each other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the פסוק means a father is not put to death by his son's testimony, and a son is not put to death by his father's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "fathers shall not be put to death for children" means by the testimony of children, and "children shall not be put to death for fathers" means by the testimony of fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the new reading: the פסוק is about witnesses. A father and son cannot testify about each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the simple meaning was already covered, the word על is read as 'through': a father is not killed through his son's words. This is the Torah source for disqualifying relatives as witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: By the testimony of
Rather, introducing the new explanation

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that relatives cannot testify comes from דברים 24:16: 'fathers shall not be put to death for children' means through the children's testimony, since the simple meaning is already taught by 'every man for his own sin.'

phrases.english: Rather, "Fathers shall not be put to death for children"
means by the testimony of children,
and "children shall not be put to death for fathers"
means by the testimony of fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים בְּעֵדוּת בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 by reading the פסוק as being about testimony.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that fathers and sons cannot testify against each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base source in the Torah for the entire list of disqualified relatives in the משנה.

steps.title: But the Torah says children are punished for fathers' sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that children are not punished for their fathers' sins, quoting the פסוק 'visiting the sin of fathers on children.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And children are not punished for the sin of fathers? But it is written: "Visiting the sin of fathers upon children"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions a part of the ברייתא: it assumed children are never punished for their fathers' sins, but another פסוק seems to say they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's logic rested on 'every man for his own sin' already teaching that children are not punished for fathers. But שמות 34:7 says God punishes children for the sins of fathers, so that simple meaning seems wrong, which would weaken the whole derivation.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? Introduces a contradicting פסוק
Visiting the sin of fathers upon children

phrases.english: And children are not punished for the sin of fathers?
But isn't it written:
"Visiting the sin of fathers upon children"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 19 that children are never punished for their fathers' sins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that children are not punished for the sin of fathers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in שמות says God visits the sin of fathers upon children, which seems to contradict the simple meaning the ברייתא relied on.

steps.title: Children are punished only when they continue their parents' ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'פוקד עון אבות על בנים' refers to children who hold on to their parents' sinful actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the פסוק is talking about children who hold on to their parents' actions and continue them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. The פסוק about punishing children for their fathers' sins only applies when the children are doing the same sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים do not really clash. A child who keeps up his parents' sinful ways is really being punished for his own sins, which add to theirs. A child who does not copy them is not punished at all.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that other פסוק
When they hold their fathers' deeds in their hands, meaning they continue those deeds

phrases.english: There, it is when they hold
phrases.notes: 'There' means the פסוק 'פוקד עון אבות על בנים' from step 21.

phrases.english: their fathers' deeds in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by limiting the פסוק to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging פסוק (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פוקד עון אבות על בנים' seems to say children are always punished for their fathers' sins, which contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Children are punished only when they continue their fathers' sinful actions, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'ואף בעונות אבותם אתם ימקו' as applying only when the children continue their fathers' deeds, and proves this from 'איש בחטאו יומתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And also in the sins of their fathers they shall waste away with them' means when they hold on to their fathers' deeds. You say it means when they hold on to them, but maybe it means even when they do not? When the Torah says 'Each man shall be put to death for his own sin,' it shows the first פסוק must mean when they hold on to their fathers' deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as its answer. Another פסוק about children suffering for their fathers' sins is limited to children who continue those sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks whether the limit is really needed. Maybe children are punished even if they do not sin. It answers no, because 'איש בחטאו יומתו' says each person dies only for his own sin, so the punishment must apply only to children who copy their fathers.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
They will waste away
You say this, or perhaps it is only that? (a ברייתא formula that tests a reading)
Each man shall be put to death for his own sin

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And also in the sins of their fathers they shall waste away with them' –
this is when they hold their fathers' deeds in their hands.
You say it is when they hold on to them,
or perhaps it is even when they do not hold on to them?
When it says 'Each man shall be put to death for his own sin,'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16, the same פסוק from step 18.

phrases.english: then it must be when they hold their fathers' deeds in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 with a ברייתא that makes the same distinction.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that children are punished for their fathers' sins only when they continue those sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 26:39, which proves its point from דברים 24:16.

steps.title: But all Jews are responsible for one another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from 'וכשלו איש באחיו', which teaches that people stumble because of each other's sins, since all Jews are ערבים for one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are people not punished for others' sins unless they copy them? But it is written: 'And they shall stumble, one man over his brother,' meaning one man because of his brother's sin. This teaches that all of them are guarantors for one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a person is only punished for sins he actually takes part in. A פסוק seems to show that Jews suffer for each other's sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 22-23 said punishment requires the person to share in the sin. But 'וכשלו איש באחיו' is read as one person stumbling because of another's sin, without any mention of copying it. The reason given is that every Jew is a guarantor for every other Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so? But it is written! (a formula for challenging from a פסוק)
And they shall stumble
Guarantors for one another, responsible for each other

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about fathers and sons anymore. The פסוק talks about any Jew suffering for another Jew's sin, which is an even wider idea.

phrases.english: And is it not so? But it is written:
phrases.notes: He means: are people really never punished for others' sins unless they copy them?

phrases.english: 'And they shall stumble, one man over his brother' –
one man because of his brother's sin,
this teaches that all of them are guarantors for one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from steps 22-23 that a person is punished only when he shares in the sin.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person is punished for another's sin only when he holds on to those actions himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'וכשלו איש באחיו' teaches that Jews suffer for each other's sins because they are ערבים, with no condition that they copied the sin.

steps.title: Responsibility comes from failing to protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'וכשלו איש באחיו' applies when people could have protested the sin and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about people who had the power to protest and did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. People are punished for others' sins only if they could have stopped them by protesting and did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of ערבות does not punish innocent people. A person who could have protested and stayed quiet has done something wrong himself. So everyone is still punished only for his own failing, and this fits 'איש בחטאו יומתו'.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest, to object to a wrongdoing
And they did not protest

steps.whatToRemember: A person is never punished for someone else's sin unless he has some guilt of his own. This can come from continuing the sin, as with children who keep up their parents' ways, or from staying silent when he could have protested, which is the meaning of ערבות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the well-known idea 'כל ישראל ערבים זה בזה'. It means each Jew is responsible to protest wrongdoing when he is able to.

phrases.english: There, it is when it was in their power
to protest, and they did not protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, שֶׁהָיָה בְּיָדָם לִמְחוֹת וְלֹא מִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by limiting 'וכשלו איש באחיו' to people who could have protested.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging פסוק (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וכשלו איש באחיו' seems to mean people are punished for others' sins even with no guilt of their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: People are punished only when they could have protested the sin and failed to, which is their own wrongdoing.
